title: The fish who overheard Shiva
hookLine: Shiva teaches Parvati the secret of yoga on a lonely shore, and a fish in the water hears every word
carry: the seals that wake the goddess within
tomorrow: Why join your palms for God and for Nani?

lines: SHIVA TEACHES PARVATI ON A LONELY SHORE.
cards: A lonely shore. Shiva is teaching Parvati the secret of yoga: how the body itself can become a path to God. In one telling, Parvati drifts off to sleep.
But someone is still listening. In the water just off the shore, a fish, or in some versions a boy swallowed by one, has heard every word.
When Shiva notices, he blesses the listener, who becomes Matsyendranath, the lord of fish, remembered as the first human teacher of hatha yoga.

teach.h: THE BOOK BOWS FIRST TO SHIVA.
teach.b: The Nath yogis tell this story, and the Hatha Yoga Pradipika, the old hatha manual, keeps its spirit. It opens with a bow to Adinatha, the first lord, a name for Shiva, as the one who taught hatha yoga.
Its list of masters begins with Adinatha and then Matsyendra. In this tradition, hatha yoga comes from Shiva. Its third chapter is on the mudras.
In Sanskrit, mudra can mean a seal, a stamp. The chapter begins with a picture. In paraphrase: as the lord of serpents holds up the earth, so all the practices of yoga rest on kundalini.
Then it says why the seals matter.

teach.h: THE GODDESS ASLEEP AT BRAHMAN'S DOOR.
teach.b: In paraphrase: the goddess lies asleep at the door of Brahman, so practice the mudras with every effort to wake her. That's the teaching.

Many Hindu traditions hold that Shakti, the divine power, lives in the body itself, coiled and asleep, and hatha teachers describe the path as waking her to rise and meet Shiva. The body isn't in the way of God.
It's where Shiva and Shakti meet.

The mudras in that chapter are whole-body seals, not finger shapes: mahamudra, the great seal, with one heel pressed in, the other leg stretched out, the hands holding the foot, the chin drawn down; and the bandhas, locks at the throat, the belly and the root.
The text guards them as secret, and they are learned from a teacher, not from a page.
So when a class today calls hatha just stretching, the book begins somewhere else: with Shiva, and a goddess waiting to wake.

how: In hatha yoga, mudras such as mahamudra and the bandhas are learned from a teacher as whole-body practices; the Nath tradition honors Shiva as Adinatha, the first teacher, and Matsyendranath as the first human guru.

games.q: you're the fish off the shore, and you've heard Shiva teach Parvati the secret of yoga. what happens next, in the story?
o: Shiva blesses you, and you become the first teacher.
you forget it all by morning.
games.why: in the Nath telling, the listener becomes Matsyendranath, lord of fish, remembered as the first human teacher of hatha yoga.

practice: Sit upright on a cushion or a chair, spine tall, hands resting on the knees. Draw the chin down just a little, without strain, and let the whole body settle into one steady shape, like a seal pressed into wax.
Leave the great seal and the stronger locks for a teacher. If you pray, bow inwardly to Shiva, the first teacher, with Om Namah Shivaya; if not, simply rest in the shape and the breath.

wordCard.voice: The mudras. Seals: shapes of the hands or the whole body, which the hatha texts say help wake the goddess asleep within.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: mudra, a seal, a stamp, a sign. Used for shapes of the hands and of the whole body.
